findings.title: Removal listener gated on V1 flag and breaks on V2
findings.body: The listener is now wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ). When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled the Role/Client/Group removal cleanup never runs, leaking authorization resources/policies. When V1 is enabled but the realm uses V2, management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled() dispatches to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, so a client/role/group delete will throw out of the provider event listener.

findings.title: Per-client check never falls back to all-clients permission and can NPE
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) loads the per-client resource and if it exists evaluates only that resource. A caller with a valid all-clients (resource-type) grant is then denied whenever any per-client resource happens to exist for that client. Conversely when the per-client resource does not exist it loads the type resource without null-checking it, so findByResource(server,null) / resource.getScopes() can NPE if the Clients type resource is missing.

findings.title: getScope NPEs on unknown/null resourceType
findings.body: getScope() does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that the map entry exists. An unknown or null resourceType causes NullPointerException instead of the intended ModelValidationException, breaking REST validation for bad resource types.

findings.title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases Users (All users vs username lookup) but has no branch for Clients. Client permissions therefore fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for FGAP resources whose name is the client UUID, so UI/API display names for client permissions are wrong/null where Users correctly resolves to username.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can return aggregate resource name
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission() iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and adds every granted resource.getName(). That includes the aggregate Clients type resource itself (named Clients) if granted, so callers filtering clients by ID get a bogus Clients entry mixed with real client UUIDs.
